liquidLevelIntro: One of Autolejek's features is support for a liquid level detector. A signal from the sensor can stop the entire process, protecting the installation from operating in unsafe conditions.
liquidLevelLowerText: Consider a water tank with a pump inside it. A sensor installed near the bottom allows Autolejek to switch the pump off when the water level becomes too low. This prevents dry running and helps protect the pump from damage.
liquidLevelLowerImageAlt: Liquid level sensor installed near the bottom of a water tank to protect the pump from dry running
liquidLevelLowerImageCaption: A sensor near the bottom of the tank detects a low water level so Autolejek can stop the pump.
liquidLevelUpperText: The sensor can also be installed near the top of the tank. When the maximum level is reached, Autolejek stops the process and prevents the water from overflowing.
liquidLevelSignalText: The sensor should use a 5 V supply and provide Autolejek with a digital high or low state. In the configuration, the user selects which signal state should stop the system. This setting must match the operation and wiring of the particular sensor.
liquidLevelFailSafeText: After wiring the sensor, simulate both of its states and confirm that Autolejek stops the process in the intended condition. Where the sensor permits, choose logic that also stops the system if its cable is broken or the sensor loses power.
liquidLevelTypesIntro: Liquid levels can be detected in several ways. Sensors differ in operating principle, mounting method, and signal type. The right choice depends on factors including the liquid, tank material, available space, and required accuracy.
liquidLevelFloatText: A float sensor is installed inside the tank at the selected height. A change in liquid level moves a magnetic float, which opens or closes a reed contact. This type is simple and needs no separate power supply, but it contacts the liquid directly. Its materials, seals, operating temperature, and mounting method must suit the specific installation.
liquidLevelFloatImageAlt: Passive float-type liquid-level sensor with two wires
liquidLevelFloatImageCaption: Example of a passive float-type liquid-level sensor.
liquidLevelUltrasonicText: Non-contact sensors detect the level without immersing a measuring element in the liquid. The example shown is a capacitive sensor installed on the outside of a tank. It detects a change in electrical properties when liquid appears behind the wall. Performance depends on the liquid and on the tank material and wall thickness; this type usually does not work through a metal wall. Ultrasonic sensors form another group and are commonly installed above the liquid surface to measure distance from a reflected signal.
liquidLevelUltrasonicImageAlt: Non-contact liquid-level sensor installed on the outside of a tank
liquidLevelUltrasonicImageCaption: Example of non-contact liquid-level monitoring through a tank wall.
liquidLevelNonContactChoiceText: They are not the same type of sensor. A capacitive sensor detects liquid at a specific point through a suitable tank wall. An ultrasonic sensor can measure the distance to the liquid surface but requires a suitable mounting location and an unobstructed signal path. Always consult the selected model's documentation.
liquidLevelSelectionRule: Before purchasing a sensor, check its supply voltage, output type, active-state logic, and compatibility with the liquid and tank.
